statement: For $x \ne 0$, which of the following is equivalent to $\dfrac{12x^4 - 8x^3 + 4x^2}{4x^2}$?

choices.misconception: I thought $4x^2 \div 4x^2$ was $0$, so the last term disappeared.
I added the exponents when dividing, instead of subtracting them.
I divided only the coefficients by 4 and left the powers of $x$ unchanged.

hints: Divide each term of the numerator by $4x^2$ separately.
Divide the coefficients and subtract the exponents, using $\tfrac{x^a}{x^b} = x^{a - b}$.

solutions.reliable: Split the fraction: $\tfrac{12x^4}{4x^2} - \tfrac{8x^3}{4x^2} + \tfrac{4x^2}{4x^2} = 3x^2 - 2x + 1$. Check by multiplying back: $4x^2(3x^2 - 2x + 1) = 12x^4 - 8x^3 + 4x^2$.
solutions.elegant: Factor the numerator as $4x^2(3x^2 - 2x + 1)$ and cancel the $4x^2$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
